issues.legal_issue: A bona fide family arrangement may be valid and binding even when the parties do not have conflicting legal claims to the property.
material_facts: The property had been acquired by the father, who directed that the younger, more capable son should receive a larger share in recognition of his contribution to the family.
After the father’s death, the younger son managed the family properties and businesses on the elder son’s promise that the father’s direction would be respected.
The younger son sought partition, and a substantial amount of property stood in his name, creating a possibility that he would claim it as his own.
To preserve family harmony and secure the younger son’s continued management, the brothers agreed that the elder’s branch would receive two shares and the younger’s branch three shares.
The courts below found that the agreement was genuine and bona fide, and the Supreme Court upheld those findings.
issues.conclusion: The arrangement was a valid family arrangement and was binding on the family members.
issues.legal_principle: Although conflicting legal claims, actual or anticipated, are generally relevant to a family arrangement, they are not essential. Bona fide disputes or apprehensions, including ones that do not involve legal claims, can suffice when family members arrange matters to preserve peace or harmony. Courts favour arrangements that are bona fide and fair in the circumstances. The Court relied on Halsbury’s Laws of England, Ram Nirunjun Singh v. Prayag Singh, Basantakumar Basu v. Ramshankar Ray, Thakur Umrao Singh v. Thakur Lachman Singh, M. Ramayya v. U. Lakshmayya, and Sahu Madho Das v. Mukand Ram.

rule.if: family_arrangement_challenge and family_members_arranged_property and bona_fide_arrangement and (existing_or_possible_dispute or family_peace_or_harmony_purpose)

predicates.family_arrangement_challenge: A party in a dispute over a family arrangement challenges whether that arrangement is valid or binding.
predicates.family_members_arranged_property: Members of the same family agreed on how family property or interests in it would be allocated.
predicates.bona_fide_arrangement: The family members made the arrangement honestly and its terms were fair in the circumstances.
predicates.existing_or_possible_dispute: The parties faced an actual dispute or a genuine possibility of disagreement over property or its management.
predicates.family_peace_or_harmony_purpose: The arrangement was made to preserve family peace or harmony or to avoid future disputes.

issues.definition: When family members honestly and fairly arrange property to address an actual or possible dispute or to preserve family peace, the arrangement is binding.

issues.legal_issue: A written family arrangement requires registration when it itself creates or transfers an interest in immovable property in the present, but not when it only sets terms for a possible future partition.
material_facts: The written agreement provided for the family to remain joint and for the parties to continue managing the property as before.
It set the shares to be taken if and when a partition occurred in the future.
It did not divide the property by metes and bounds, sever the parties’ status, or otherwise affect their interests in immovable property in the present.
issues.conclusion: The agreement did not require registration.
issues.legal_principle: Section 17(1)(b) of the Registration Act applies where an instrument itself creates, declares, assigns, limits, or extinguishes an interest in immovable property in the present. The Court distinguished Thakur Umrao Singh v. Thakur Lachman Singh, where the instrument was intended to effect an immediate partition, and considered Rajangam Ayyar v. Rajangam Ayyar and, by analogy, Hari Sankar Paul v. Kedar Nath Saha.

rule.if: family_arrangement_registration_dispute and written_family_arrangement and partition_only_in_future and no_present_property_interest_created

predicates.family_arrangement_registration_dispute: A party disputes whether a written family arrangement must be registered.
predicates.written_family_arrangement: The family arrangement is recorded in a written instrument.
predicates.partition_only_in_future: The instrument provides for shares to apply only if a partition takes place later and does not itself effect a partition.
predicates.no_present_property_interest_created: The instrument does not itself create, transfer, or alter an interest in immovable property in the present.

issues.definition: A written family arrangement that leaves the family undivided and only sets terms for a possible later partition does not require registration if it creates no present property interest.

issues.legal_issue: A court does not uphold an unpleaded family arrangement when it accepts one of the alternative arrangements expressly pleaded and put in issue.
material_facts: The defendant pleaded both an arrangement with the plaintiff’s father and an alternative arrangement with the plaintiff’s mother after the father’s death.
The trial court framed separate issues addressing whether each arrangement was true, valid, and binding.
The courts below accepted the arrangement with the father, which was recorded in the written agreement, and rejected the alternative arrangement with the mother.
issues.conclusion: The courts below accepted the first of the two pleaded arrangements, not a different or unpleaded arrangement.
issues.legal_principle: The Court examined the written pleadings and the issues framed on them and concluded that the finding rested on an arrangement expressly pleaded and tried under a separate issue.

rule.if: civil_appeal_challenging_family_arrangement_finding and alternative_arrangements_pleaded and issues_framed_on_those_arrangements and court_accepted_one_pleaded_arrangement

predicates.civil_appeal_challenging_family_arrangem: A civil appeal challenges a court’s finding about a family arrangement.
predicates.alternative_arrangements_pleaded: A party’s pleadings set out more than one possible family arrangement.
predicates.issues_framed_on_those_arrangements: The court framed issues addressing whether the pleaded arrangements were true, valid, and binding.
predicates.court_accepted_one_pleaded_arrangement: The court accepted one arrangement that had been expressly pleaded.

issues.definition: When alternative family arrangements are pleaded, issues are framed on them, and the court accepts one of them, the accepted arrangement was pleaded.
